name: CortexDynamics Stratum Entertainment BCI
description:
The CortexDynamics Stratum is a consumer BCI engineered around immersive entertainment and neural gaming, offering a standard feed and civic integration platform augmented by the company's ImmersCore neural entertainment engine. The ImmersCore module expands the BCI's sensory processing channels beyond standard AR overlay into partial sensory substitution territory — while falling well short of full-immersion military or luxury systems, the Stratum can deliver enhanced spatial audio directly to the auditory cortex, proprioceptive feedback for physical gaming applications, and a deep-feed mode that prioritizes entertainment signal processing at the cost of background feed functions, creating a noticeably richer immersive experience than standard consumer BCIs. The platform runs at 150 Mbps with an eight-channel architecture — four dedicated to standard feed operations and four switchable to ImmersCore entertainment processing — with 1440p AR rendering and a 6ms latency profile that competitive gaming communities have benchmarked favorably. Standard civic integration, QUANTA payment, and full feed access are included, and the Stratum supports optional smartlink unlock for carry permit holders.

The Stratum has carved out a devoted following among GLMZ's gaming subcultures, neural entertainment communities, and the sprawling population of Tier 2-3 residents who treat immersive entertainment as a primary social outlet in a city where physical recreation space is scarce and expensive. Neural gaming leagues — particularly the underground tactile combat simulation circuits that operate in warehouse spaces throughout the outer Tier 2 districts — have effectively standardized on the Stratum as their preferred hardware, and CortexDynamics sponsors several semi-professional teams. The device has a complicated relationship with mental health advocates, who note that the deep-feed mode's sensory richness creates measurable dependency profiles in vulnerable users — the city's neural addiction support services report that Stratum units account for a disproportionate share of entertainment-dependency cases, a statistic CortexDynamics contests vigorously in its public filings.
legality: Unrestricted — deep-feed mode subject to GLMZ Neural Entertainment Use guidelines; not legally restricted but flagged in therapeutic contexts
installation_requirements: Outpatient procedure at CortexDynamics authorized clinic or independent neural installer; local anesthetic; 2-hour installation; ImmersCore calibration session 48 hours post-install
rejection_risk: Low to Moderate — standard mesh integration is low-risk, but ImmersCore's expanded sensory processing channels require additional neural pathway mapping that shows elevated inflammatory response in approximately 8% of patients during the first month
maintenance: Bi-weekly automatic firmware updates; ImmersCore sensory calibration recommended every six months as neural pathways adapt to the enhanced processing load; deep-feed mode usage logging recommended for users with dependency risk factors

cultural_context: The Stratum sits at an interesting cultural intersection: it is genuinely excellent hardware for its price point, but its association with entertainment dependency and gaming subcultures gives it a slightly disreputable reputation in professional Tier 3 circles. Corporate HR departments in conservative firms have been known to flag Stratum implants in background checks as a lifestyle signal — an informal association with people who prioritize escapism over ambition. In the outer Tier 2 districts and the Shelf's upper edges, however, the Stratum is aspirational hardware, and the neural gaming communities that have formed around it represent some of the most tight-knit social networks in the city. The ImmersCore dependency statistics have made the device a flashpoint in ongoing legislative debates about neural entertainment regulation.

story_hooks: A pirated ImmersCore content package circulating through underground neural gaming networks in the outer Tier 2 districts contains something extra — a passive data-harvesting routine that is collecting not just usage data but raw sensory memories from deep-feed sessions, and the content itself seems designed to elicit specific emotional states worth recording.

A player character discovers that a close contact has slipped into severe neural entertainment dependency — their Stratum's deep-feed logs show they haven't voluntarily exited the ImmersCore network in eleven days, sustained by automated civic services that are somehow still processing their QUANTA payments. Someone is keeping them in.

CortexDynamics is preparing to push a mandatory firmware update that will throttle deep-feed mode intensity by 40% in response to new city neural health regulations — and the underground gaming community is planning to riot, while a grey-market firmware vendor is offering a patch that preserves full ImmersCore functionality at the cost of removing all safety limiters.
